def test_add_elements():
    # Basic case: first k elements with at most 2 characters in their string form
    assert add_elements([1, -2, -3, 11, 0], 3) == 1  # -2 and -3 have '-' sign, excluded
    assert add_elements([111, 21, 3, 4000, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9], 4) == 24  # 21 + 3
    assert add_elements([111, 121], 2) == 0  # all have 3 digits

    # All elements within limit
    assert add_elements([1, 2, 3, 4], 4) == 10
    assert add_elements([10, 20, 99], 3) == 129

    # k larger than array length: only available elements considered
    assert add_elements([5, 10], 5) == 15

    # k = 0 yields empty slice
    assert add_elements([1, 2, 3], 0) == 0

    # Empty array
    assert add_elements([], 3) == 0

    # Negative numbers: '-' sign counts toward string length
    assert add_elements([-5, 7], 2) == 7        # "-5" has length 3, excluded
    assert add_elements([-11, 22], 2) == 22     # "-11" has length 3, excluded
    assert add_elements([-99, -100, 50], 3) == 50

    # Single element cases
    assert add_elements([100], 1) == 0
    assert add_elements([9], 1) == 9

    # Boundary: exactly 2-character strings (e.g., 10..99) are included
    assert add_elements([10, 99, 100, 9], 4) == 10 + 99 + 9
